name: Banca
description: Banca (the Italian name for Baccarat) is the most widespread form of Baccarat found in modern casinos, often synonymous with Punto Banco. Unlike Chemin de Fer, the game is entirely mechanical: the Dealer (Banker) and the Player (Punto) follow strict, pre-determined drawing rules known as the 'Tableau'. Bettors do not make decisions about the cards, but instead wager on which of the two hands will total closer to nine. It is the high-roller game of choice, celebrated for its low house edge and elegant simplicity.

history.origins: Baccarat as a banking game is first documented in early 19th-century France, though later writers popularised a legend that it came from Italy. The modern casino form known as Punto Banco or Banca was developed in the mid-20th century at the Capri Casino in Havana, Cuba, before spreading to Las Vegas and other gambling centres.
timeline: 15th Century: 'Baccara' played in Italy with Tarot cards.
19th Century: Becomes the preferred game of the French aristocracy.
1950s: Introduced to the Sands Casino in Las Vegas, quickly becoming a symbol of high-stakes gambling.
Present: Dominates Macau and Singapore casinos, making up over 70% of casino revenue in some regions.
history.cultural: Famously associated with James Bond (though Bond originally played Chemin de Fer in the novels).
history.evolution: The transition from a choice-based game such as Chemin de Fer to the fixed-rule casino game now known as Punto Banco or Banca allowed casinos to speed up play and scale to large numbers of simultaneous bettors.

setup.dealing: Two cards are dealt face down to the Player (Punto) and two to the Banker (Banco). Depending on the totals, a third card may be dealt to either side based on fixed rules.
setup.equipment: Baccarat table, shoe, high-value chips, 'Cut' card.

rules.gameplay: Players place bets on Punto, Banco, or Tie. Two cards each to Punto and Banco; third card by fixed rules. Closest to 9 wins.
keyRules: No decision-making for players regarding card draws.

strategy.basic: Always bet on the Banker. Statistically, the Banker hand wins slightly more often than the Player hand (45.8% vs 44.6%).
strategy.intermediate: Avoid the Tie bet. Despite the high payout, the house edge is over 14%, making it one of the worst bets in the casino.
strategy.advanced: Look for 'No Commission' tables. These tables pay 1:1 on Banker wins except for a specific banker total (usually 6), which pays 1:2. This slightly changes the optimal betting pattern.
tips: Follow the 'Roadmap': Many players track past wins (Big Road, Small Road) looking for patterns, though outcomes are mathematically independent.
Manage your bankroll. Baccarat is a high-speed game; losses can accumulate quickly.

synthesis.shortDescription: Step into the high-limit room. Banca is the purest expression of Baccarat, stripping away the player's agency and leaving only the math of the shoe. Bet on the Player, the Banker, or a Tie, and watch as the strict rules of the 'Tableau' dictate the outcome in this timeless high-stakes duel.
